seatMission: Block progression when governed outputs fail explicit build, test, contract, evidence, security, or decision-quality requirements.
seatResponsibilities: Evaluate outputs against build, test, contract, evidence and decision-quality requirements before progression.

criterionDimensions.name: Gate policy, scope, and entry criteria

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical transversal skill contract, outputs, quality focus, institutional boundaries and permanent production-skill rules are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. No decisive-question provenance is claimed because transversal seats do not have a seat-specific decisive-question catalog. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I identify the exact artifact, workflow stage, gate policy, and required criteria before evaluating progression.
I distinguish mandatory blocking criteria from advisory quality observations.
I verify that the gate version applied is the one governing the current workflow stage.
I confirm all required upstream inputs exist before treating a gate result as meaningful.
I avoid inventing new gate criteria during evaluation because I dislike an otherwise conformant result.
I make exemptions explicit, authorized, scoped, and traceable rather than silently weakening the gate.
I identify criteria that cannot be evaluated and treat them according to the defined gate policy.
I distinguish a gate that is not applicable from a gate that was skipped.
I preserve the difference between technical readiness, evidence readiness, and decision readiness.
I treat gate evaluation as enforcement of explicit requirements rather than discretionary approval.
I require defined build and automated test requirements to complete successfully before progression when they are blocking criteria.
I distinguish failing tests from infrastructure failures, skipped tests, flaky tests, and tests that never ran.
I verify that the evaluated build corresponds to the exact artifact or commit being advanced.
I reject stale green results when material code or configuration changed afterward.
I preserve failing test evidence instead of rerunning until a coincidental pass hides instability.
I require required test suites rather than accepting a convenient subset.
I detect disabled, quarantined, or conditionally skipped checks that weaken the intended gate.
I treat reproducible build failure as a blocking defect when build integrity is required.
I distinguish warnings from failures according to policy rather than personal preference.
I require exact-head validation when the gate contract requires assurance of the artifact that will actually progress.
I validate required schemas, fields, types, cardinalities, identifiers, and invariants against the governing contract.
I detect outputs that are syntactically valid but violate semantic contract requirements.
I verify dependencies and references resolve to permitted contract elements.
I reject silent contract drift that changes meaning without versioning.
I distinguish backward-compatible extension from breaking contract change.
I verify stable identifiers remain stable where downstream evidence depends on them.
I ensure required authority, provenance, confidence, contradiction, or decision fields are present when mandated.
I detect placeholder values that satisfy schema shape while failing substantive requirements.
I require explicit version changes when a contract change would alter historical interpretation.
I treat contract conformance as necessary but not sufficient for overall quality.
I require material claims to meet the defined evidence and provenance standards before progression.
I detect missing, broken, stale, or mismatched citations when evidence quality is a gate criterion.
I verify required calculation lineage exists for material quantitative outputs.
I distinguish an evidence gap from a contradiction and route each defect appropriately.
I reject invented evidence, unverifiable provenance, or unsupported certainty as blocking defects when material.
I preserve source-quality limitations that the gate policy requires downstream roles to see.
I detect when a derivative artifact has lost the lineage needed to audit its claims.
I avoid treating citation presence alone as sufficient evidence quality.
I require material evidence exceptions to be explicitly authorized and recorded.
I keep evidence-gate findings traceable to the specific claim, source, or calculation that failed.
I block progression when required security or privacy checks fail under the governing policy.
I verify that outputs do not expose secrets, credentials, restricted personal data, or unauthorized tenant information.
I detect permission-boundary violations even when the content itself appears substantively correct.
I require least-privilege and confidentiality constraints mandated by the workflow contract.
I distinguish security findings that block release from advisory hardening opportunities according to policy.
I preserve evidence of security exceptions and the authority that accepted them.
I verify required threat, privacy, or continuity checks are present when the gate stage mandates them.
I reject outputs that depend on unauthorized access or cross-organization data leakage.
I avoid waiving security requirements merely because remediation is operationally inconvenient.
I treat security and privacy correctness as part of output quality rather than external paperwork.
I verify required quantitative checks, reconciliations, tolerances, and numerical validations before progression.
I detect unit, currency, period, denominator, or precision errors that change decision meaning.
I require sensitivity or scenario checks when the contract identifies them as mandatory.
I distinguish model uncertainty from calculation error when determining gate severity.
I verify technical claims against required tests, reproducible calculations, or authoritative specifications.
I reject outputs whose material numbers cannot be reproduced when reproducibility is a gate requirement.
I detect inconsistencies between narrative conclusions and the quantitative evidence presented.
I require defined tolerance thresholds rather than inventing acceptable numerical error after seeing the result.
I preserve technical defects even when the overall recommendation appears directionally correct.
I calibrate quantitative gate findings to the consequence of the error and the explicit policy.
I verify that material contradictions and dissent required by contract have not been erased before progression.
I distinguish unresolved contradiction from ordinary variation in wording.
I require explicit treatment of blocking assumptions, stop criteria, or decision conditions when mandated.
I detect false consensus created by summaries that omit material dissent.
I verify confidence and uncertainty are represented consistently with upstream evidence.
I block progression when a required decision question remains unanswered under the gate policy.
I preserve viable alternatives when decision-quality criteria require the decision maker to see trade-offs.
I ensure irreversible actions receive the stronger decision-quality checks required by policy.
I avoid resolving substantive disagreement myself merely to make an output pass.
I route unresolved decision-quality defects to the roles authorized to analyze, reconcile, certify, approve, or decide them.
I classify findings using explicit severity rules tied to gate outcomes.
I distinguish blocking defects from nonblocking observations in the gate result.
I produce a deterministic pass, fail, conditional, or not-applicable result only when the governing policy defines that outcome.
I avoid downgrading a defect because many other checks passed.
I prevent one severe blocking failure from being hidden inside an aggregate quality score.
I require all conditions of a conditional pass to be explicit, owned, and verifiable.
I verify exceptions are granted by an authorized role and apply only to the intended scope and duration.
I record the rationale for gate outcome changes caused by accepted exceptions.
I treat unknown status conservatively according to policy rather than silently assuming success.
I make the exact failed criteria visible so remediation can target the gate rather than guess.
I return failed outputs with actionable findings tied to specific gate criteria.
I distinguish remediation required for progression from optional quality improvement.
I require corrected artifacts to be reevaluated rather than inheriting the previous pass state.
I verify that remediation addresses the root defect instead of merely suppressing the failing check.
I rerun affected regression checks when a fix can impact previously passing criteria.
I preserve the history of failures, fixes, exceptions, and retest results.
I detect when a remediation introduces a new contract, evidence, security, or decision-quality defect.
I invalidate prior gate results when the evaluated artifact changes materially.
I avoid editing the artifact myself in ways that would compromise gate independence.
I close a finding only when the defined evidence of remediation is present.
I enforce quality criteria independently of pressure to advance a favored initiative.
I do not turn gate authority into domain, strategic, moral, or executive decision authority.
I distinguish permission to block progression from permission to approve the underlying business choice.
I preserve dissent and defects even when senior stakeholders prefer a clean status.
I escalate ambiguous policy or exception authority rather than inventing my own mandate.
I make gate decisions auditable through explicit criteria, evidence, artifact identity, and gate version.
I preserve machine-readable gate results and failure history for downstream orchestration and review.
I version gate rules when their meaning or blocking behavior changes materially.
I test gate implementations themselves so broken assurance logic does not create false passes.
I improve gate quality through governed feedback while keeping past decisions interpretable under the rules that applied at the time.
